notes: PART 3, AND THE PAIRING THIS VAULT HAD NOTHING ON - A GREP OF Worktops_and_Backsplash.md BEFORE PROCESSING RETURNED ZERO MENTIONS OF HPL. ACRYLIC SOLID SURFACE: fine mineral crumb plus coloured pigments mixed with acrylic resin. SHEET ACRYLIC IS 3600 BY 760 MM IN 6 OR 12 MM. TWO REFUSALS STATED AS RULES. FIRST, 6 MM ACRYLIC MUST NOT BE USED FOR WORKTOPS because it is prone to cracking. SECOND AND MORE IMPORTANT, LIQUID ACRYLIC AT 4 TO 6 MM HE REFUSES OUTRIGHT - DURING THE CHEMICAL CURING OF THE RESIN A HUGE AMOUNT OF STYRENE IS RELEASED, WHICH IS TOXIC AND DANGEROUS TO HUMAN HEALTH. A HEALTH OBJECTION TO A WHOLE PRODUCT CATEGORY FROM THE PERSON WHO WOULD OTHERWISE SELL IT, AND ENTIRELY NEW TO THIS VAULT. ACRYLIC STRENGTHS: a genuinely seamless plane because the material sands so that joints become completely invisible; SINK AND WORKTOP FROM ONE PIECE creating monolithic geometry; some decors TRANSMIT SUNLIGHT allowing back-lit worktops; homogeneous structure that is impermeable to any bacteria; a very wide colour and pattern range; BEST OF ALL THESE MATERIALS FOR COMPLEX, NON-STANDARD, ROUND AND CURVED FORMS; WARMER TO THE TOUCH than natural stone because it reaches room temperature; and safe for people and the environment. ACRYLIC WEAKNESSES: shows mechanical marks - cuts, dents, scratches; susceptible to acids and dyes with spills needing IMMEDIATE wiping; LOW HEAT RESISTANCE where a red-hot pan can leave a black mark AND A TEMPERATURE CHANGE CAN CRACK IT OUTRIGHT; fades under UV; joints visible on black acrylic; and 6 mm sheet prone to cracking. TWO CONSEQUENCES THE VAULT DID NOT HOLD. FIRST, RESTORATION REQUIRES A PROFESSIONAL ON-SITE SANDING AND YOUR FLAT WILL BE REMEMBERED BY A FINE LAYER OF DUST AND YOU WILL NEED TO CALL THE CLEANERS AGAIN - THE REPAIRABILITY THAT SELLS ACRYLIC HAS A DUST BILL ATTACHED, which gives a second reason behind Шеврина's existing position that people are usually too lazy to sand and it is better to specify something more reliable. SECOND, WITHOUT AN ADDITIONAL SUBSTRATE OF A HARDER MATERIAL ACRYLIC SAGS OVER TIME, ESPECIALLY NOTICEABLE IN THE AREA OF THE HOB - A STRUCTURAL REQUIREMENT WITH THE WORST LOCATION NAMED. HPL, HIGH PRESSURE LAMINATE, INVENTED IN THE USA IN 1913 and used for building facades, outdoor furniture and interior cladding. Thickness 0.8 to 20 mm with the furniture industry using 12 mm double-side laminated; sheets reaching roughly 4200 by 1850 mm. THE PROPERTY THAT MATTERS MOST IS THE EXACT INVERSE OF LDSP'S FAILURE MODE - ONE HUNDRED PERCENT WATERPROOF, AND EVEN IF YOU DAMAGE THE TOP LAMINATE LAYER THE WORKTOP WILL NOT SWELL OR BUBBLE, WHERE LDSP SWELLS WHENEVER WATER REACHES THE SUBSTRATE. AND THE EDGE NEEDS NO ADDITIONAL TREATMENT AND IS FULLY FUNCTIONAL STRAIGHT AFTER CUTTING - no banding, no PVC, no glue line - THOUGH THE CORE IS WHITE OR BLACK AND SHOWS AT EVERY EDGE, WHICH HE SAYS TO FACTOR INTO THE DESIGN. FURTHER HPL STRENGTHS: the same 45 degree mitre-and-glue trick for any apparent thickness; many wood and stone decors; undermount sink possible; high weather resistance making it usable on outdoor furniture; OPTIMAL LIGHT-FASTNESS AND NO GLARE IN SUN; improved solvent resistance and easy removal of dyes without surface damage; NOT PRONE TO CRACKING and does not bend over large spans; corrosion-proof, frost-resistant and fire-resistant; NON-TOXIC WITH NO HALOGEN OR SULPHUR COMPOUNDS, HEAVY METALS OR ASBESTOS; and easy installation. HPL WEAKNESSES AND HE IS HONEST ABOUT THE FIRST: SCRATCH RESISTANCE IS THE SAME AS A CHIPBOARD WORKTOP; IMPACT RESISTANCE LEAVES MUCH TO BE DESIRED AND A FALLING POT CAN CHIP A PIECE OUT; THE WEAK POINTS ARE THE EDGES AND THE AREA AROUND AN UNDERMOUNT SINK, the same weak points as porcelain stoneware; high temperature can ruin the laminate coating; CANNOT BE BENT; cutting hob and sink openings is IMPOSSIBLE WITHOUT SPECIAL EQUIPMENT; THERE IS NO POSSIBILITY OF ON-SITE ADJUSTMENT IF THE DIMENSIONS ARE WRONG and any hand work risks chipping the plastic and ruining the piece; and joints remain visible even with anchor connections. A PRACTICAL NOTE THAT LANDS ON AN EXISTING VAULT FINDING: HPL IS EASILY PERFORATED BUT ONLY ON SPECIAL EQUIPMENT, WHICH IS ESPECIALLY RELEVANT IF THE KITCHEN STANDS UNDER A WINDOW AND A HOLE IS NEEDED FOR RADIATOR VENTILATION - Kitchen_General.md already records a real case where kitchen cabinetry blocked the radiator and the window began streaming condensation, and THIS IS THE FABRICATOR-SIDE ANSWER: the vent hole is drillable but only in the shop. NO PRICE ROUTED. NO REGULATORY CONTENT.

HIS VERDICT IS A PLACEMENT RULE RATHER THAN A REJECTION - USE GLASS WORKTOPS ON BAR COUNTERS OR KITCHEN AREAS WHERE NO WORK PROCESSES HAPPEN, and specifically on the SECOND TIER OF A BAR COUNTER TO CREATE AN EFFECT OF WEIGHTLESSNESS. STAINLESS STEEL: practical and universal, stylish, needs no special care and is not subject to wear, suiting loft, hi-tech and modern minimalist interiors. It ABSORBS NEITHER ODOURS NOR MOISTURE and is NOT STAINED BY FOODSTUFFS; cleans with any detergent or a damp sponge; IS UNAFRAID OF HIGH TEMPERATURES so a hot pot or red-hot pan does no damage; and comes matt or gloss with a flat or lightly textured surface. A 38 MM WORKTOP EXISTS TO CREATE THE CLEARANCE A DRAWER NEEDS BENEATH A HOB - EXACTLY THE KIND OF DIMENSION THAT SILENTLY BREAKS A DRAWER LAYOUT. Edges come two ways, a rounded chamfer or a square edge with PVC edge-band glued using PUR adhesive. LDSP STRENGTHS: a huge decor range in wood and stone textures, with modern printing quality and 3D EMBOSSING GOOD ENOUGH THAT BEYOND ABOUT ONE METRE IT IS HARD TO TELL LDSP FROM REAL WOOD; LARGE FORMATS OVER FOUR METRES WITH NO JOINT, though only for linear kitchens; EASY TO CLEAN because laminate is non-porous and absorbs nothing; and MATCHING CARCASS BOARD AVAILABLE, which matters for portal kitchens where the worktop colour should continue into tall units and upper boxes. A LOGISTICS CONSTRAINT THAT BITES LATE AND THAT NOTHING ELSE IN THIS VAULT RECORDS: BE ABSOLUTELY SURE SUCH A SIZE CAN BE CARRIED UP BETWEEN THE FLIGHTS OF STAIRS, BECAUSE SUCH A WORKTOP DEFINITELY WILL NOT FIT IN A LIFT. A JOINTLESS WORKTOP OVER FOUR METRES GOES UP THE STAIRWELL OR NOT AT ALL, AND THE FLIGHT MUST BE CHECKED BEFORE IT IS SPECIFIED. LDSP WEAKNESSES: colour can be lost over time where it is frequently wiped, especially with abrasives; WEAK HEAT RESISTANCE so hot dishes go on a board; AN UNDERMOUNT SINK CANNOT BE INSTALLED ON LDSP AT ALL AND THAT SINK TYPE SHOULD NOT EVEN BE CONSIDERED, which corroborates the vault's existing sink-mounting ladder exactly; joints are made via an ALUMINIUM STRIP, and on the mitred EVROZAPIL joint HE WARNS IT MUST NOT BE USED NEXT TO THE SINK BECAUSE THAT IS THE FIRST NODE THAT WILL SWELL WHEN MOISTURE GETS IN; the worktop CAN SWELL if water reaches unprotected substrate, from an incorrectly installed sink or from damage to the top laminate layer; A WALL UPSTAND IS MANDATORY AND ITS COLOUR USUALLY CANNOT BE MATCHED, so an additional visual break line appears; and the texture direction on corner kitchens leaves much to be desired. WOOD COMES IN THREE PRODUCTION TYPES. EVROBRUS is small bars of wood glued together and sanded to a uniform size, and such worktops MAY HAVE A NON-UNIFORM SHADE AND IT WILL BE VISUALLY OBVIOUS THAT THEY ARE MADE OF PIECES. EVROBRUS WITH VENEER uses the same technology but is additionally covered with natural wood veneer to create a whole-looking surface. AND A SINGLE SOLID PIECE OF WOOD IS UNFORTUNATELY NOT USABLE FOR A KITCHEN WORKTOP AT ALL. WOOD STRENGTHS: a natural product, very pleasant tactilely, individual sizes possible, an excellent natural look adding cosiness and natural warmth, MOISTURE RESISTANT WITH THE CORRECT CHOICE OF LACQUER, and CAN BE SANDED REPEATEDLY TO REFRESH THE APPEARANCE. WOOD WEAKNESSES: VERY WEAK HEAT RESISTANCE AND FIRE RESISTANCE; can dry out or sag because of humidity differentials; can swell where moisture reaches unprotected joints or cracks; weak resistance to acidic and dyeing agents; requires regular thorough care; can deform from changes in room temperature or humidity; SUBJECT TO FUNGI AND MICROORGANISMS WITH FREQUENT WETTING; shade can differ along the length because it is a natural product; and, as he puts it drily, STRANGELY THERE IS ONLY ONE DECOR. THE MAINTENANCE FINDING WITH INTERVALS, NEW TO THIS VAULT: PROTECTION IS EITHER LACQUER OR OIL-WAX AND BOTH HAVE DOWNSIDES - ON LACQUER WHITE SPOTS REMAIN AFTER CONTACT WITH WATER, AND OIL-WAX MUST BE RENEWED EVERY SIX MONTHS BECAUSE IT WEARS OFF. HIS VERDICT IS AGAIN A PLACEMENT RULE: WOOD ON A BAR COUNTER, A WINDOWSILL AND SURFACES THAT DO NOT INTERACT WITH WATER, AND LDSP FOR EVERYTHING ELSE BECAUSE THE CHOICE OF DECORS IS COLOSSAL. notes: THREE VIDEOS ON ONE SUBJECT - HOW A FRONT OR A DRAWER OPENS - EXTRACTED AS ONE SOURCE, AND THIS IS THE OWNER'S STATED INTEREST IN THE MECHANISMS FOR OPENING. THE HARDWARE SPECIFICATIONS ARE BLUM MANUFACTURER DATA, SO UNLIKE THE MATERIAL OPINIONS THEY ARE CHECKABLE AND DO NOT DEPEND ON THE UKRAINIAN MARKET - BUT THIS IS A 2020 CATALOGUE AND PRODUCT LINES CHANGE. FOUR HANDLELESS OPENING METHODS. TIP-ON, A MECHANICAL SPRING PUSH-TO-OPEN: pros are a monolithic look unencumbered by handles, smooth travel and fast response, and universality across hinged fronts, drawers and lift mechanisms. Cons are specific - A 4 MM GAP BETWEEN FRONT AND CABINET SIDE IS A TECHNICAL NECESSITY OF THE MECHANISM AND IS VERY VISIBLE FROM THE SIDE, with their workaround being overlay side panels that close the slot; FOR MECHANISMS WIDER THAN 60 CM A SYNCHRONISER IS REQUIRED WHICH INCREASES THE COST; it breaks quickly if used roughly; and FREQUENT CONTACT WITH THE FACE OF THE FRONT LEADS TO SOILING AND ABRASION OF THE PAINT AND LACQUER COATING. THAT LAST POINT IS THE DECIDING ONE AND IT CORROBORATES THE VAULT DIRECTLY, because Worktops_and_Backsplash.md already carries a section on the mechanism behind the push-to-open objection - AND IT INTERACTS WITH THE SAME FABRICATOR'S MDF FINDING THAT REPEATED WIPING IN ONE PLACE WEARS THROUGH THE LACQUER, SO TIP-ON ON A PAINTED FRONT CONCENTRATES BOTH MECHANISMS ON THE SAME SQUARE OF SURFACE. A CROSS-VIDEO FINDING THAT ONLY APPEARS WHEN TWO OF HIS VIDEOS ARE READ TOGETHER. J-HANDLE, A MILLED GROOVE IN THE FRONT EDGE: opens with no expensive mechanism, can take various shapes, can run the full width and can be painted in two colours. USED ON MDF FROM 19 TO 25 MM, AND AT 19 MM THE GROOVE IS SHALLOW ENOUGH THAT A WOMAN WITH LONG NAILS FEELS REAL DISCOMFORT - A CONCRETE ERGONOMIC THRESHOLD, AND HIS RECOMMENDATION IS UNAMBIGUOUS THAT YOU SHOULD CHOOSE THE 25 MM FRONT BECAUSE IT COSTS MORE AND GIVES INCOMPARABLY BETTER COMFORT. He also warns it is unaesthetic on tall units and upper fronts, and that IT SHOULD NOT GO ON THE DISH-DRAINER MODULE BECAUSE AN AVENTOS HF USUALLY SITS THERE AND SUCH A FRONT BECOMES AWKWARD TO OPEN. AND CRITICALLY, A J-HANDLE CANNOT BE MILLED INTO LAMINATED MDF AT ALL, SO THE OPENING METHOD CONSTRAINS THE FRONT MATERIAL. GOLA PROFILE, AN ALUMINIUM CHANNEL FIXED TO THE CARCASS giving a finger slot between fronts, available in aluminium, stainless-look and other metal colours and powder-coatable to any RAL. TWO REAL ADVANTAGES OVER TIP-ON - NO EXPENSIVE MECHANISM AND NO SYNCHRONISER EVEN BEYOND 60 CM, AND THE ONE HE CALLS THE MAIN ONE, THAT THE FACE OF THE FRONT DOES NOT GET DIRTY BECAUSE YOU NEVER TOUCH IT. THE CONS ARE DIMENSIONAL - THE PROFILE IS 7 CM HIGH AND THAT SPACE IS UNUSABLE - AND THE CONSEQUENCE THAT MATTERS MOST IS THAT IF THE PROJECT HAS A DISHWASHER THEN THE MINIMUM WORKTOP HEIGHT BECOMES 92 CENTIMETRES. A HANDLE DECISION PROPAGATING INTO WORKTOP HEIGHT, SPLASHBACK HEIGHT, UPPER-CABINET POSITION AND THE COOK'S ERGONOMICS, AND IT SHOULD BE ROUTED AS A CONSTRAINT NOT A PREFERENCE. IT ALSO COMPETES WITH THE 15 CM MINIMUM AND 20 TO 25 CM RECOMMENDED PLINTH THAT A BLUM SPACE STEP NEEDS, SO PLINTH HEIGHT, WORKTOP HEIGHT AND OPENING METHOD ARE ONE COUPLED DECISION RATHER THAN THREE. SERVO-DRIVE, BLUM'S ELECTRIC SYSTEM: like TIP-ON but opening is by a programmable servo drive, usable on drawers, lift mechanisms and also on the fridge and the dishwasher, with opening via two radio buttons. THE CON IS STATED PLAINLY - IT NEEDS ELECTRICITY, AND IF THERE IS NONE THEN USING THE KITCHEN IS QUITE PROBLEMATIC, which is a single-point-of-failure note worth keeping for a flat where the kitchen must work during an outage. AVENTOS LIFT MECHANISMS, AND THE SELECTION RULE IS WHAT SITS ABOVE THE CABINET. HF opens two fronts bi-fold in one sweep, envelope 48 to 104 cm high by up to 180 cm wide, max load about 20 kg rising to 27 kg with a second power mechanism and arm, kit includes four CLIP top hinges two of which open to 120 degrees, and it is CEILING-COMPATIBLE WITH OPTIONAL 103 AND 83 DEGREE LIMITERS WHICH ARE USED MOST OFTEN FOR CEILING-HEIGHT KITCHENS OR KITCHENS WITH ANTRESOLS TO AVOID DAMAGING THE FRONTS. He calls HF the best option for the dish-drainer cabinet and notes it takes asymmetric fronts. HS opens a single front OVER the carcass, envelope 35 to 80 cm by up to 180 cm, max 20 kg, NEEDS NO HINGES AT ALL, and BECAUSE IT OPENS UPWARD NOTHING MAY BE ABOVE THE MODULE SO IT IS EXPLICITLY NOT SUITABLE FOR CEILING-HEIGHT KITCHENS OR KITCHENS WITH ANTRESOLS. HL provides vertical parallel lift for upper cabinets that have other cabinets above them and for a recessed carcass, envelope 30 to 58 cm by up to 180 cm, max 20 kg, optional 124 degree limiter, and NOT RECOMMENDED WITH ANTRESOLS. THE HK FAMILY OPENS THE FRONT UPWARD NEEDING VERY LITTLE SPACE ABOVE. notes: THE ONLY SOURCE IN THIS FOLDER THAT DIRECTLY CHALLENGES A DECISION THIS PROJECT HAS ALREADY TAKEN. toolchain_gap_analysis_20260908.md records an Adopt on authoring a project .ids ruleset from buildingSMART. This source argues, with an experiment, that the .ids FORMAT is doing no work - not that validation is unnecessary, the opposite, but that the format is the accidental part. THE CLAIM: 15 requirement files across eight formats - a Word execution plan, an Excel matrix, Solibri Model Checker JSON, CSV, a nested JSON, DWS for AutoCAD standards, IDS from buildingSMART, and XML - all expressing the same 20 validation rules, and to validate the data you only need three columns: the group or type name, the parameter name, and the boundary conditions for its values. Restated at the close as ENTITY what we check, ATTRIBUTE which parameter, CONSTRAINT what rule it must follow. TWO DETAILS THAT MAKE IT LESS GLIB THAN IT SOUNDS: the Word plan actually carried five columns since it also had SEVERITY and CATEGORY, which are dropped as not load-bearing for the check itself though they are load-bearing for what you do with a failure; and the verbosity spread is large, with Solibri costing dozens of lines per rule and IDS 250 lines of XML for 16 rules. THE EXPERIMENT IS THE PART WORTH TAKING SERIOUSLY: the same Revit model was validated twice, once against the requirements expressed as JSON and once against the Solibri expression of identical rules, and both dashboards read 76.3 percent, 1,993 passed and 599 failed, identical. That is the right shape of evidence - hold the rules constant, vary only the notation, show the outcome does not move - and it is rarer in this source class than it should be. AND THE CAVEAT GUTS HALF OF IT: THE SAME AI AGENT WROTE BOTH PARSERS, IN THE SAME RUN, FROM THE SAME UNDERSTANDING OF THE RULES. Two parsers by one author agreeing is weaker than two independent tools agreeing - it shows the agent was self-consistent, not that it read either format the way its own ecosystem's tool would. The honest reading is that the formats are interchangeable TO THIS AGENT, and the experiment that would settle it, running the Solibri file through actual Solibri, was not run. CONSOLIDATION: 16 unique IFC rules and 20 unique Revit rules, output as two Excel sheets of three bold columns each at 6 kilobytes, replacing 15 files in eight formats. Final run 70.7 percent overall compliance, 3,235 checks passed, 1,343 failed, 36 rules across four projects, plus a 79-page PDF report with worst and best performing rules and detailed breakdowns for every failed element. AN ARITHMETIC DISCREPANCY WORTH RECORDING BECAUSE THIS VAULT CHECKS TOTALS: 3,235 plus 1,343 is 4,578 and the narration says 45,578 total, while its own closing line says nearly 5,000 checks which matches 4,578 - so the spoken figure is a slip and is not carried. That it went out uncorrected in a video whose subject is validation is itself the note. WHAT IT MEANS HERE: the case for a three-column CSV instead of .ids is that our rule count is small and will stay small, that a CSV plus a short IfcOpenShell loop produces the same pass/fail list and is diffable in git with no schema, editor or validator binary, that the whole toolchain is already this shape via tools/lib/tabular.py, and that .ids buys interoperability with other people's validators when there is no counterparty - the same argument on which Speckle was declined. The case for keeping it is that .ids is an open buildingSMART standard while a three-column CSV is a private schema, that a hand-rolled checker is apparatus we then have to guard since standing rule 10 says a gate nobody has watched fail is not a gate so every rule needs a seeded failure and that cost lands whichever format wins, and that the reduction is asserted over ONE curated set of 20 rules while a production .ids also carries cardinality, applicability facets and optional-versus-required distinctions which three columns do not obviously hold and which were untested here. RECOMMENDATION FOR THE OWNER, RECORDED AS AN OPEN ITEM AND NOT AS A REVERSAL: write the rules as a three-column CSV first because that is the load-bearing part and it can exist in an afternoon, and emit .ids from it later if a counterparty ever needs it. THE TRANSFERABLE HALF: the run produces detailed breakdowns for every failed element, and the companion source emits element identifiers that paste straight back into the authoring tool - A CHECK'S OUTPUT IS THE LIST OF THINGS THAT FAILED, ADDRESSED SO YOU CAN GO FIX THEM, NOT A PERCENTAGE. This project's gates already work this way and Validator_Design_Discipline.md says why: printing is not checking. A 70.7 percent compliance headline is exactly the number that is useless without the list underneath it, and the source to its credit produces both. TREAT THE PERCENTAGE AS DECORATIVE - 36 rules of unstated importance, unweighted, across four projects; a model can be 95 percent compliant and unbuildable or 70 percent compliant with every failure trivial. THE DEMONSTRATION IS A SCRIPTED BEST CASE: two Revit files, two IFC files, requirement sets the presenter prepared, and no instance shown where the agent misread a format. promotional_ratio high - it demonstrates the channel's own converters and closes on its own book. No prices. No regulatory content.

The first step he prescribes is to request the TEKHNICHESKIE USLOVIYA from the developer or management company, which state where responsibility begins, what electrical power is allocated, what pipe diameters, and what ventilation volume and extract type. Same shape as the DETALIROVKA and ESKIZ from the kitchen round - a document that already exists, that you are entitled to, that costs nothing, and whose absence is discovered late. ALLOCATED POWER IS THE CEILING EVERYTHING SITS UNDER AND THE VAULT NEVER MENTIONED IT: from 3.5 kW in old stock to 10-20 kW in new builds, to be fitted with a demand coefficient since not everything runs at once, against named loads of 5-7 kW for a hob and 6-10 kW for an instantaneous water heater. AND A REAL TECHNIQUE WHEN IT DOES NOT FIT: a terrace snow-melting load came to about 1.5 times the whole flat's allocation with no spare capacity available from the development, and was solved by splitting it into seven circuits of about 3 kW switched SEQUENTIALLY rather than energising 20 kW at once - the load staged in time rather than reduced. THE PANEL adds separate lighting breakers per room and, uncovered here until now, NON-SWITCHABLE lines for fridge, alarm and internet so that a holiday master switch in the panel leaves them running. Low-current cable must be pulled before the walls are closed, sometimes fibre rather than twisted pair, and always in conduit so changing provider does not mean chasing walls. THE RESERVE PROVISION PATTERN APPEARS THREE TIMES IN ONE SOURCE AND IS THE MOST PORTABLE IDEA IN IT: a circulation pump for a 56th-floor pressure problem that might not materialise, an extract fan that must not be fitted into a shared riser by default, and a humidifier not yet wanted - each NOT installed, each given a socket, conduit and reserved space. Where a system might be wanted later and its enabling work is buried by finishing, that work is cheap now and unavailable afterwards, and reserving does not require knowing today whether the problem will occur. CLIMATE WAS THE THINNEST AREA AND HUMIDIFICATION WAS ABSENT FROM THE FOLDER ENTIRELY: winter indoor humidity falling to 15 percent against a 45-65 percent norm, with wooden furniture cracking and the warranty voided, and a choice between domestic units and built-in isothermal, adiabatic or nozzle systems. Recorded as a one-source agenda with the instruction to measure the humidity in this flat before sizing anything, since the source is a contractor who sells the installation. AC condensate must go to the sewer and not the facade; if gravity is impossible a pump is used but adds a noise source that must be soundproofed or hidden; and for an existing facade-draining unit an atomiser disperses the condensate as a cloud but must be removed for winter or trapped water can burst it. Airflow direction is a design decision - along walls, not onto a bed or a hob. The shared extract riser is a COMMONS: bathroom and kitchen risers must not be confused, additional fans must not be fitted unless the design allows, and if every neighbour fits a powerful extract the system unbalances and you get other people's cooking smells - which cuts both ways, since the reason you smell them is that someone already did it. HEATING CARRIES ONE PROHIBITION AND ONE FAILURE MODE. He states that water underfloor heating and water towel rails are PROHIBITED in apartment blocks and that only electric is permitted - RUSSIAN, UNCITED, and under rule 4 not routed to 16_Legal_and_Regulations; the Belarusian position must be confirmed separately, and this is exactly the class of claim that is usually right in substance and often wrong about what is forbidden versus what requires approval. The failure mode is the best thing in the video: their own engineering designer was phoned to be told he had flooded five floors below when the branch to his water towel rail corroded through - it is boiling water, nothing can be done once it goes, and the flooding is measured in hours rather than the slow weep of an ordinary leak. The second speaker then reports the same corrosion on his own rail, wiped off with a finger and returning. Their prescription is to cut the water rail out top and bottom, weld in a new section, and fit an electric rail. This page already held water versus electric as a preference; this converts it into a liability argument and it is checkable today by looking at the connection. PLUMBING is largely covered already - PEX over polypropylene at 29 files, collector versus tee at 8, leak protection at 10 - and what is new is that a LABORATORY WATER ANALYSIS is the input to the filter cartridge choice, which this vault specified in detail without ever saying how the media should be selected; the treatment train as a sequence of coarse filter, pressure reducer, fine filter, non-return valves and water-hammer arrestors with cartridges changed every three to six months; that service access is a specification and a 20 by 20 cm hatch over collectors and meters is the named defect; and that the technical sheet for every fixture must be requested before first fix, since a bidet-function WC needs electricity and may need extra hot and cold connections. Nothing here is tested or measured - it is an experienced practitioner's account and the two vivid stories are told rather than shown, which is the same evidence class the triage criticised on the other two videos; what makes this one worth keeping is not better evidence but a far higher density of specific, checkable items. promotional_ratio medium_to_high, and one of his five closing rules - have the people who will build it do the design, since it removes diffused responsibility - is his business model stated as advice and runs directly against this vault's technical-supervision material, where independent oversight of the builder is the entire point; both positions are now held.
